behavior: Reads the acknowledged descriptor through a NextOwner request/response interface; no activation exponent is supplied through configuration.

Joins original root, input rank, kept rank and tag, requires post-attention normalization and ordinary-prefill context, and derives checked shifts from signed exponents and immutable bucket/fallback policy.
Drives the existing row-frame configuration interface and retains a maximum down-output unit plus its matching scale-table address; the saturated legacy residual writer stays disabled.
Retains one logical frame lease across sequential kept ranks; final release requires successful completion acceptance and output drainage.

Preserves offered requests, configurations and completions through faults. Within an active or concurrently accepted context, unassociated responses quarantine their channel and prohibit a new completion until coupled reset.
regressions: Both unassociated descriptor-response and unsolicited compute-terminal bugs failed in the original hardware simulation before the fix and passed afterward.
Cases cover bucket/fallback selection, negative gain, shift63 and overflow admission, output exponent374, wrong normalization role, mismatched tags, skipped ranks, early release and stalled offers.
limits: These simulations use synthetic descriptor and compute endpoints. The real frame parent, normalization source, trained assets and compute arrays were not executed by this case.
Source bytes were compiled from identical private copies. No clean-checkout replay or synthesis is claimed.
Resource limits were set by the recorded launch commands; native kernel limits were not independently probed.
Per-channel units require actual matching table decrements. An asset identifier alone does not authenticate payloads.
